thread:
Morgan: Heads-up: our dependency scanner flagged CVE-2026-4512 in libfastkv (client-side KV lib). Public PoC just landed; exploitability looks moderate. Need to decide patch window and whether to notify affected customers. SLA impact if we do an immediate hotfix: expected 2-4h degraded throughput on Dedicated during canary. Thoughts?

Sam: Link to the advisory and PoC?

Morgan: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/CVE-2026-4512 and https://gist.github.com/anon/poc-libfastkv — PoC targets an unauth admin path on older agents.

Tara: Thanks. Quick triage: appears to only reach the admin HTTP endpoint if agent is configured with legacy admin API enabled. Most Hosted and recent Dedicated images default to admin disabled.

Alex: If that's true, blast radius is lower. But we should still treat as high priority since PoC exists and some customers run older agents. Suggest: canary -> 03:00 UTC window, 30m canary, then staged rollout over 6-12h. Ops: @Irina will this cause measurable capacity or SLA hits?

Irina: Canary will touch 1 GPU pool for the migration and rolling restarts. Expect short perf hit (~10-15% qps) for ~30m while caches warm. If we schedule during 03:00 UTC, impact on customer latency minimal. We'll still call it a degraded-throughput window in the incident page.

Morgan: Customer tiering question: notify Enterprise/Dedicated and Private customers immediately or wait until we confirm exploit attempts? Pro/Free hosted customers?

Sam: Draft plan: notify Dedicated & Private customers pre-patch with mitigation steps. For hosted customers, send notice only if we detect exploit activity or if backups fail. I'll prepare email templates and provide review.

Tara: Running audit grep now for 'unauth-admin' and related patterns across last 72h. Will post counts in 5m.

Tara: audit results: 6 unique external IPs with attempts in past 48h, 0 successful auth bypasses, all blocked by current firewall rules. Looks like scanning.

Alex: Given scanning activity, push timeline forward. Actionable plan: 1) enable temporary WAF rule to block PoC pattern 2) canary tonight 03:00 UTC 3) staged rollout over 6h 4) proactive emails to Dedicated/Private customers. Also prepare rollback plan and perf dashboards.

Morgan: Agreed. Let's keep the canary tight: 30m pilot, verify metrics (error rate, p95 latency, throughput). Action items:
- Tara: enable WAF rule + confirm audit logs
- Irina: schedule canary 03:00 UTC and reserve pool (notify infra)
- Sam: draft customer notice for Dedicated/Private
- Alex: prepare rollback playbook and dashboard queries (token-level cost, p50/p95, active KV sessions)

Irina: Canary scheduled in internal calendar. I'll post deploy-bot notice 30m before.

deploy-bot: irina scheduled canary deploy for 2130018000 (03:00 UTC window), target pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-2.

Morgan: Thanks all. We'll re-evaluate at T+30m during canary and update incident channel. :thumbsup:
